Adam and Eve are the first human beings in biblical tradition. According to Genesis, God created them and placed them in the Garden of Eden, where they lived in paradise with just one restriction: they could not eat from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Adam was created first directly from the earth as the image of God, and Eve was created from one of his ribs to be his companion. When the serpent tempted Eve with the forbidden fruit, promising she would become like God, she ate it and gave it to Adam as well. This disobedience triggered what's called the Fall of Man. They were expelled from paradise and lost their immortality, condemned to a life of labor and suffering. Eve is often blamed in traditional theology for humanity's downfall, though her role reveals something more complex: she represents both creation and transgression. Their sons Cain and Abel went on to represent humanity's first moral conflict, with Cain murdering his brother Abel in jealousy. In Christian theology, Adam is called the First Adam, and Jesus becomes the Second Adam, who reverses the damage of the fall through redemption.
